Steffan, Oscar,

I compiled a list of all the negative issues I have found to check with you
if I might be overlooking something.
If that's the case, we can clarify at our meeting today.
Also, it would be good to know if any of the issues are planned to be
addressed on your roadmap

Daniel

*Missing basic features:*

   - No gallery view for datasets (it is possible for folders but not for
   datasets)
   - No dataset statistics: how many files / GB in a dataset?
   - No operations on datasets (filter, split into subsets, statistics) - a
   dataset is just a group of files, we need to use 1:1 matching between
   folders and datasets because we can explore folders
   - No direct support for setting up a project where part of the data is
   labelled by over 1 annotator (consensus), plus annotation quality
   statistics (workaround exists that requires setting up two projects, but
   statistics need to be computed by us). Also, we then cannot analyse
   statistics for the full dataset since the data is splitted by two projects
   - No conditional validation of the annotations (requires post-processing
   of the exported data, resulting in back and forward or eliminating invalid
   annotations)
   - No option for numerical inputs, only text (would be good to have
   validation if it is integer, or define valid range, date/numeric masks, or
   a regex)
   - No option for annotating tags / keywords (checkbox exists but should
   not be a good option when the number of tags is high)
   - Difficult to track what classes were already entered when annotating
   (no visual cues)
   - No video level annotations (annotations are frame level, we get more
   data than needed, and it adds a frame selection step to the annotation).

subject: AW: Further Questions on Annotations
text:
Hi Steffen,

Here is a quick reply to your Delivery Lead's questions:

  1.
What do you mean by different hands? It would be great if you could go into more detail of what he means and how it could be a time sink.
We want to label bounding boxes for all visible hands, but do not care about left/right or which person it belongs to. If both hands overlap it would also be fine to mark it as one.
  2.
We can't provide you with a reference time at this point in time.
  3.
- For product bounding boxes we require consistent IDs for the same instance of the product. Two milk cartons would have different IDs, but the same milk carton should get the same ID again after being hidden and reappearing. Every other class (hand, barcode, etc.) can have a random unique ID, we could even deal with having no IDs for those.
- For data protection regulations we have to anonymize faces in our recordings before saving. Sometimes our face detection makes errors and anonymizes products or random areas in the frames. Since we don't have those effects during inference, we don't want those frames in our training data. What we require is a way to determine those frames, which in V7 is a tag "falsely_pixelated" that is attached to the whole frame. Since we're not using this frame for training, we don't require (but accept) any labels for them, just to save labeling time.

Hope that helps. If you have any further questions, please reach out.

Best regards | Mit freundlichen Grüßen
